chi2.what: chi2 = sum z^2, bound chi2_{nu,0.95}: 18.31 for the ten pair-days, 11.07 for a pair's five. sigma_f: prespecified = 1.25 s_f / sqrt(n); idle_noise_only = the idle test's parametric bootstrap (sensitivity.py); no_f_term = sigma_M from the simulator's noise alone. The decision is the WL fit with the prespecified sigma_f; the rest was chosen after the run.

pool.rule: Eq. (pool), run.py: weights w_i = 1 / sigma_O,i^2 over the ten pair-days (WL); error sqrt(max(1, chi2_0 / nu) / sum w), chi2_0 = sum w (Lambda_i - Lambda)^2, nu = 9; d = 5 worse if Lambda + t_{nu,0.95} se < 1, better if Lambda - t se > 1. The pooled prediction uses the same weights.

sigma_f.what: prespecified sigma_f = 1.25 s_f / sqrt(n), the standard error of a median from the spread of the job's n per-qubit f; idle_noise sigma_f = sd of the median over 2000 parametric redraws of the idle test (sensitivity.py); ratio = idle_noise / prespecified

per_qubit_fits_overdispersed.what: each qubit-job's line in run._fit_share (Eq. S5): weighted residual chi2 at the fitted f, dof = idle lengths kept - 2. Uniformity = run._uniformity's chi2/nu about the inverse-variance mean f, then with each qubit's sigma times sqrt(max(1, chi2/dof)), qubits with no dof unscaled. The prespecified tests use sigma_f = 1.25 s_f / sqrt(n), which does not involve these per-qubit sigmas.

windows.what: plain means over each pair's five days of Lambda_X, device and model (the prediction at the measured f), both curves fitted on the same window by the same fit (sensitivity.py). Systematic = half the range over the ten choices below; rounds 3-8 are left out because there the distance-5 P(n) is 0.38-0.51 throughout and Lambda_X mostly noise.

table_pairs.convention: plain means over the five days. Error sqrt(sum sigma_i^2) / 5, times sqrt(chi2_0 / 4) when chi2_0 / 4 > 1, chi2_0 = sum ((v_i - mean) / sigma_i)^2, for observations and predictions alike. Observed sigma_i: each fit's own (WL delta method in X memory and the WL bootstrap sd in Z memory, binomial profile), as effect_sizes.py. Predicted sigma_i: the test's sigma_M with the prespecified sigma_f (and, in X memory, with the noise-only sigma_f as a check). For pair 1's Lambda_X the widened prediction error is the calibration's change from day to day, not the uncertainty of one prediction.

power.what: the same miss in every pair-day (WL, the prespecified fit); sigma_i = sqrt(sigma_O^2 + sigma_M^2). One pair-day: P(|z| >= 2) at a Lambda_X miss of 0.06. A pair: noncentral chi2, 5 dof, bound 11.07. All ten: noncentral chi2, 10 dof, bound 18.31, noncentrality sum (miss / sigma_i)^2; and the miss found with 80% probability.
